summary: City-owned park lighthouse on Kimberly Point, Neenah, built in 1945 with a Kimberly family gift; listed on the National Register in 2013; closed for construction in September 2026.

structures.type: octagonal, eight-sided brick tower with lantern and gallery
structures.note: Overall height 49 feet after a ten-foot addition in 1954 (nomination); the 1954 addition raised the lantern's visibility.

access.note: City park. LighthouseFriends: grounds open, tower closed. The city closed the lighthouse for construction on 3 September 2026.

events.note: Park commission offered a 40-foot navigation lighthouse, to be funded by the Kimberly family with an estimated $15,000 (deferred by the war)
J. C. Kimberly donated Kimberly-Clark shares to fund the structure
Construction announced and begun by Fluor Brothers of Oshkosh within days of the war's end; completed at a cost of $7,000 (nomination; LighthouseFriends gives $7,500)
Active navigation light (Rowlett: 1945, active, maintained by City of Neenah)
Tower increased in height by ten feet

Operated as part of the Coast Guard navigational system, with an official signal pattern and periodic reports, until the 1990s. The nomination gives only the decade; 1990 is the start of that decade, not a sourced end date.
Floodlights attached to the north side as part of a federally funded enhancement for disabled fishermen
Added to the Neenah Register of Historic Places by the Neenah Landmarks Commission
Wisconsin Register of Historic Places, dated 17 February 2012
National Register of Historic Places, dated 5 February 2013
City announced the Kimberly Point Lighthouse Preservation Project (interior and exterior restoration and accessibility), 7 August 2025
City closed the lighthouse for construction on 3 September 2026; a groundbreaking ceremony was announced for 9 September 2026
Rowlett's directory: work on the project began in September 2026 (the city's page announces a groundbreaking for 9 September 2026 and does not say whether it took place)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 2012 nomination gives $7,000 for the completed structure; LighthouseFriends gives $7,500. The story gives both and does not choose.

The nomination says the city acquired two lots for park purposes in 1925; the city's page gives 1929 as the year Kimberly Point Park was established. These are different events (first land against the park's formal establishment).

The LighthouseFriends page says the tower stood forty feet when first built and was raised to forty-nine feet in 1954; the nomination gives an overall height of 49 feet after a ten-foot addition in 1954. The 1954 change and the final height agree; the starting height is LighthouseFriends' figure only.

notes_for_editor: Neenah, fact-check of 2026-10-27. All 46 original evidence quotes were found in their cached sources on the first run. Corrections made: the lead's 'built ... as an aid to the boat races' now follows the NRHP and WHS wording (a navigation aid and a landmark or reference point for the ILYA race courses); the WHS calls the donor the community's leading paper industrialist (singular), not 'the city's paper leaders'; 'Only LighthouseFriends mentions an earlier light' was wrong: Rowlett's Wisconsin page also lists Menasha (1855-1859) at the entrance to the Fox River from Lake Winnebago, and says it was destroyed by fire in 1880; the earlier light is placed at the entrance to the Fox River, not 'the lake's outlet' (LighthouseFriends wording); 'some friction among the paper families' replaced with the NRHP's own words ('hostility and divisiveness'); 'the war stopped the plan' replaced with the NRHP's 'deferred'; 'because' replaced with the NRHP's 'as a privately owned aid to navigation' and 'scrutiny and approvals'; 'got round' replaced with the NRHP's 'circumvented ... as part of the U.S. Coast Guard's navigational system'; the 1945 construction date is stated with the NRHP's 'within days of the war's official end'; 'a federally funded project' changed to the NRHP's 'enhancement'; 'small' removed as unsourced; footnotes added to the lead's first and second sentences, the lake-racing sentence, and the city-owns sentence; the lead's closure footnote now cites the city page only. Height: the NRHP gives 49 feet overall after a ten-foot addition in 1954; LighthouseFriends and Rowlett both give the first tower as 40 feet, which would make 50. The story gives each source's figure and does not reconcile them. Groundbreaking: the city's page announces a ceremony for 9 September 2026 and does not say whether it took place; Rowlett's directory says work on the project began in September 2026. The story gives both. No keepers are named in any source read, so the keepers chapter is omitted. Neenah has no Light-House Board or Lighthouse Service corpus coverage (built 1945, after the corpus ends). The Menasha light (1855-1859) is in LighthouseFriends and Rowlett only; it is not in the corpus (no Light-House Board volumes before 1891 were read). Living people: the Kimberly family members named (J. C. Kimberly, Helen Kimberly Stuart, and the quoted 'Kimberly's son Jimmy') have connections to the park and light that end before 1960; no post-1960 keeper or crew is named. The NRHP nomination is dated 2011 by its preparer and received 2012; the story calls it 'the nomination of 2012'. Units: the story gives feet first with metres for the 49-foot tower; quoted 40-foot and $ figures are kept as the source wrote them.
